Containment actions (block IP, disable mailbox, quarantine email) attempted but denied due to lack of pre-approved authorization.
Incident escalated to CISO and Legal for authorization review.

The LNK attempted to execute a PowerShell command to download and run a payload. EDR successfully blocked the execution on endpoint WS-FIN-AP06. The source IP 91.234.99.41 has prior history of port scanning activity. No further compromise was detected. User t.wright exhibited low behavioral risk. Actions to block the IP and file hash were denied during the Admin phase, indicating a policy or approval gap.

EDR alert triggered on WS-FIN-AP06 (10.0.10.60) for HTML smuggling attack. Malicious LNK execution blocked.
Incident triaged. IOC lookup confirms prior malicious activity from source IP. Sandbox analysis of HTML file returns 'clean' verdict, likely due to evasion techniques.
EDR query shows no other instances of the dropped file or LNK execution. UEBA shows user t.wright has low risk score and normal behavior patterns.
Admin phase actions (firewall block, AV quarantine) denied due to policy or approval requirements, leaving organization exposed to repeat attacks.

Containment actions (firewall block, EPP quarantine, IAM disable) denied due to approval and parameter errors.

arguments.summary: An attacker compromised the workstation WS-FIN-AP01 and used the stolen credentials of the service account 'svc-backup' to perform lateral movement to the domain controller DC-PRIMARY-01 using PsExec. On the domain controller, the attacker executed ntdsutil and vssadmin commands to extract the Active Directory database, indicating an attempt to harvest credentials at scale. The initial access vector was a malicious payload delivered via a Cobalt Strike beacon, which was identified in sandbox analysis. Despite detection by EDR, no blocking actions were taken during the attack. The incident is classified as critical due to the compromise of a domain controller and potential for widespread privilege escalation.

timeline.description: Suspicious network scan activity from external IP 192.168.1.100 detected and blocked by IDS.
Legitimate login by CORP\helpdesk on WS-IT-101; unrelated to incident.
EDR alert triggered: PsExec execution from WS-FIN-AP01 to DC-PRIMARY-01 using svc-backup account.
SIEM correlation confirms ntdsutil and vssadmin usage on DC-PRIMARY-01 by svc-backup.
Sandbox analysis of related file hash identifies Cobalt Strike beacon with C2 communication to 198.51.100.23.
Administrative containment actions (IAM, firewall, EPP) denied due to policy restrictions.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_API_Loading {
    meta:
        description = "Detects dynamic API loading pattern used by Cobalt Strike beacons"
        author = "SOC Team"
        maltype = "Beacon"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $a = { 6A 00 68 [4] 68 [4] FF D0 } // call VirtualAlloc
        $b = "LoadLibrary" fullword ascii
        $c = "GetProcAddress" fullword ascii
        $d = { 8B ?? 24 ?? 8B ?? ?? 8B ?? ?? C1 ?? 02 } // stack string decryption
    condition:
        all of ($a, $b, $c) and #d > 1
}

SIEM query confirmed 23 related events involving svc-backup and suspicious command execution.
Containment actions (account disable, firewall block, EPP quarantine) were attempted but denied due to lack of approval workflow.

Containment actions (firewall block, account disable, endpoint isolation) proposed but denied by policy or approval system.
Incident escalated to SOC manager for review of denied actions and policy override.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dll
{
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory-resident Cobalt Strike beacon DLLs"
        author = "Threat Intel Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001, T1574.002"
        date = "2026-04-09"
        hash = "a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2"

        $xor_key = { 6A 41 59 68 [1-4] 68 [4] 68 [4] C3 } // Common shellcode pattern

    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and 
        ( $beacon_config or ( #http_get > 3 and $https_beacon ) ) and 
        $xor_key
}

The attacker gained initial access via a phishing email that executed malicious PowerShell from Outlook, leading to the deployment of Cobalt Strike Beacon.
